examples: See exactly which files the agent's last turn touched, including files it changed through shell commands, and read each diff.
Step back through the last 20 turns of a session to find the turn that broke a file.
Check how much disk the snapshots take for each repository in Settings.
Put the files back to how they were after an earlier turn, see first exactly what changes, and undo it from the snapshot taken just before.
how_to: Open the file browser from a Claude Code terminal in a git repository and choose the changed files tab.
Pick a turn in the picker above the list: "now" is the live git status, each turn shows the files it changed against the turn before.
Click a path to read that turn's diff; files that look like secrets or are over 20 MB are never captured, and the list says how many were left out.

With a turn picked, "revert files to this point" opens a preview of what changes, comes back and gets deleted; revert is refused while another live session works in the same folder, and a snapshot of the files as they are is taken first, so "before the revert" in the picker undoes it.

In a Claude Code terminal's bookmarks popup, pick conversation, files or both beside the arm box: both rewinds the conversation first, then puts the files back to the end of the bookmarked turn; a mid-turn bookmark keeps the conversation only and its rewind key says why. A Codex session reverts its files from the changed files tab and is told in its prompt that its files went back to turn N.
Settings > general > turn checkpoints shows the snapshot count and disk use per repository.
media_exempt: needs a real Claude conversation with finished turns in a git repository; no recording is captured yet
name: Turn checkpoints
summary: a snapshot of the files at the end of every Claude Code turn that used tools, in git repos, kept in a private store that never touches your index, branch or HEAD; the file browser shows what each turn changed and can put the files back to a turn after a preview.
where: The changed files tab of the file browser, through its turn picker.
